in_hebrew.name: ולדימירה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם ולדימירה הוא נגזר מהשמות הסלאביים ולדימיר ומרה, שמשמעותם שושלת תהילה וגדולה לנצח. השם הוא הלחם של המילים ולדימיר שפירושו שליט גדול והמילה מירה שפירושתה שלום או עולם. השם ולדימירה הוא בעל משמעות עמוקה ומרמז על אישה שגדלותה ותהילתה תימשך לנצח.

in_greek.name: Βλαδιμίρα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Βλαδιμίρα προέρχεται από τα σλαβικά ονόματα Βλαδίμιρ και Μαρά, που σημαίνει δυναστεία δόξας και μεγαλοσύνης αιωνία. Το όνομα είναι σύνθετο από το Βλαδίμιρ που σημαίνει μεγάλος κυβερνήτης και το Μαρά που σημαίνει ειρήνη ή κόσμος. Το όνομα Βλαδιμίρα έχει βαθιά σημασία και υποδηλώνει μια γυναίκα της οποίας η μεγαλοσύνη και η δόξα θα διαρκέσουν αιωνία.

in_latin.name: Vladimira
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Vladimira derivatur ex nominibus slavicis Vladimirus et Mera, quae significant dynastia gloriae et magnitudinis aeterna. Nomen est compositum ex Vladimirus, quod significat magnus princeps, et Mera, quod significat pax seu mundus. Nomen Vladimira profundam significationem habet et mulierem cuius magnitudo et gloria in aeternum perseverabunt, denotat.

in_english.name: Vladimira
in_english.meaning: Eternal glory and greatness, noble ruler of peace
in_english.long_meaning: The name Vladimira originates from Slavic roots, specifically from the names Vladimir and Mera. It signifies a person of eternal glory and greatness, often associated with a noble ruler who brings peace. The name Vladimir means 'renowned prince' or 'great ruler,' and Mera means 'peace' or 'world.' Together, Vladimira represents a powerful and peaceful leader whose legacy endures. It carries a rich history and conveys strength, nobility, and serenity. In Christian tradition, names like Vladimira are chosen for their profound meanings and spiritual significance, reflecting virtues and aspirations for the child's life.

data.spiritual_significance: The name Vladimira has spiritual significance as it reminds us of the central role of Christ in ruling over the world. The first part of the name, vlad, is derived from the Slavic term for rule, while mir signifies the world. In the context of Christianity, our world is ruled by God, who holds the ultimate power and authority over all creation. The name Vladimira encourages us to acknowledge and submit to God's infinite presence and control in our lives. Thus, the name carries a subtle yet profound reminder of God's sovereignty and the importance of putting our faith in Him as the true ruler of our lives.

historical_references.reference: Vladimira of Kiev, also known as Saint Vladimira, was the sister of Prince Vladimir of Kiev, who is renowned for his religious conversion of the Rus' to Christianity in 988 AD. Vladimira was the wife of Prince Sviatoslav of Polotsk, who embraced Christianity in 989 AD. She is venerated as a patron saint of mothers and is believed to have played a significant role in the spread of Christianity in the region.

Vladimira of Galicia-Volhynia, also known as Hedwig, was the first Christian queen of Poland, ruling as regent for her underage son, Władysław Łokietek, from 1323 to 1339. She was the daughter of Prince Leo of Rutenia and was married to Casimir III the Great, King of Poland, in 1325. Her influence on her husband and her role in the politics of the time helped strengthen the position of the Polish monarchy during the period of the early 14th century.
